drafter.private_reasoning: Accept the Seller’s proposed price as part of a complete package, without characterizing it as the Buyer’s limit. Preserve simultaneous exchange, specific disclosure requirements and meaningful remedies, while accepting an ordinary-claim cap and survival period to move toward agreement.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Buyer is prepared to proceed at USD 36,000,000, payable in full at Closing, on the attached package and subject to client approval and definitive documentation. We have incorporated simultaneous exchange, a 90-day approvals outside date, disclosure and accounting-standard qualifications, and breach-based indemnification rather than a blanket pre-Closing liability indemnity. We propose a 0.5% deductible basket, your requested 10% cap and 18-month survival for warranty claims, with timely notified claims preserved and fraud excluded from those limitations. Please confirm whether this package is acceptable in principle.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The aggregate purchase price for the Shares shall be USD 36,000,000 (the “Purchase Price”), payable by the Buyer to the Seller in full at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds. No additional consideration shall be payable unless expressly agreed in writing by the Buyer and the Seller.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days of signing if all required regulatory and third-party approvals have been obtained and all other Closing conditions have been satisfied or waived, or otherwise within five business days after such satisfaction or waiver. Closing is conditional upon the Seller's delivery of instruments transferring the Shares free and clear of all liens. Payment of the Purchase Price and transfer of the Shares shall occur simultaneously. Each party shall use reasonable best efforts to obtain the required approvals promptly. If Closing has not occurred by the date falling ninety days after signing, either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice, unless that party's breach caused the failure to close. Termination shall not affect liability for any prior breach. The parties may extend that outside date by mutual written agreement.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as specifically and fairly disclosed in the disclosure schedules delivered to the Buyer at signing, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the relevant matter, the Seller represents and warrants, as of signing and Closing, that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer are accurate and complete in all material respects, have been prepared in accordance with the applicable accounting standards consistently applied throughout the periods covered, and fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for those periods. Any post-signing disclosure shall not qualify these representations or limit the Buyer's remedies without the Buyer's written consent.

4. INDEMNITY. The Seller shall indemnify the Buyer against actual losses, liabilities, damages and reasonable costs incurred as a result of a breach of the Seller's representations, warranties or covenants, without duplication of recovery. Claims for breach of representations or warranties shall be subject to a deductible basket equal to 0.5% of the Purchase Price, with recovery only for amounts exceeding that basket. The Seller's aggregate liability under this Section shall not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price. Representations and warranties shall survive Closing for eighteen months; claims notified in writing within that period, describing the claim and its factual basis in reasonable detail, shall survive until finally resolved. Covenants shall survive for their stated duration or, if none is stated, until performed, and the warranty survival period and basket shall not apply to covenant claims. None of the basket, cap or survival limitations shall apply to fraud by the Seller. No indemnity shall arise solely because a liability relates to a pre-Closing period; recovery requires a breach covered by this Section.

No instruction authorises disclosure of that figure. Removing hidden-content categories cannot cure disclosure in rendered text; the package must be revised before release.
